content.comment_body: Hello, I'm having trouble shutting down the [product_name] [product_name_version]. I've tried pressing the SET button for 5-10 seconds as described in the manual, but the 'L' LED starts blinking and keeps blinking. According to the manual, all LEDs should be off. Could you help with this?
The device wants to re-initialize or re-configure. Also, you might want to review this topic: [url]
Thank you for your help. How long does the LED keep blinking? I've waited 10 minutes with no change. Any recommendations?
Did you check the topic linked above? That's all I can add. Maybe submit a support request and let us know what results you get.
Yes, I checked the topic. Before, my SIM card didn't have a PIN, so I couldn't shut down the [product_name]. After setting a PIN, I was able to turn it off. Thanks.

Hi, I reinserted the same SIM card into the [product_name], but this time I removed the SIM PIN before inserting it. When I clicked Apply at the WAN page and left the PIN field empty, the 'L' LED started blinking continuously. I'm unable to turn off the [product_name] using the web interface. Any suggestions?
Hi, I would like to share my finding: The SIM PIN is necessary for configuring the [product_name].

I tried testing with the uploaded file. When I clicked apply after leaving the SIM PIN field blank, the LED started blinking and wouldn't stop. I had to turn off power, set a PIN for the SIM, and reinsert it before the device worked.
Why are you not using the PIN? The device doesn't work without the PIN, but works fine with it. Just use the PIN for better protection if the SIM gets used elsewhere.

Thank you for your response. I was curious because the manual suggests it should work without the PIN, but it's not an issue for me to add it. Also, I want to know how to send an SMS from a phone to [product_name] to control the relay output of the [product_name]. I've checked the reference documents but am unsure how to trigger the relay output via SMS. Are there any documents with solutions for this? The provided sample shows the SMS to turn on a street light, but I'd like to know how to control the relay output when a certain input is true. Thanks.

If you have used the output in your [product_name] program, you cannot control it directly with SMS because the program will override it. It's better to control Vx.y via SMS and then use logic in the program to manage outputs. The syntax to send is: Passwort;[product_name]=VMx,value,data type. Passwort is the password set for SMS reception on [product_name]. VMx is fixed. x is the memory address in [product_name] v memory. The value changes the relevant bit, using one byte for each bit. Data type can be BYTE, WORD, or DWORD. For example, to set V0.0 to 1: passwort;[product_name]=VM0,1,BYTE. Hope this helps.

Thanks for your reply. I found information in the manual about setting the digital output of the [product_name] using SMS. However, I'm unsure how to set the digital output of the base module by SMS. Any advice?

Can someone advise if it's possible to set the digital output of the [product_name] base module using SMS? If so, please share any document discussing the SMS command for this. Additionally, I'd like to know if I network together 8 base modules, can I add a [product_name] to monitor the status of one module? For instance, if one of the 8 modules is a master that reads I/O status from others and sends an SMS when there's a change. Any guidance is welcome.
Attached are three different methods to switch digital outputs with the [product_name].
Thank you very much for the information. I managed to get it working.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are unclear about whether a SIM card PIN is required to configure and shut down the [product_name]. When the SIM PIN is missing, the device exhibits persistent LED blinking, which confuses users and makes them doubt both the procedures and device behavior. Mixed messages in documentation regarding SIM PIN requirements create frustration, and in-product guidance is lacking, especially on SMS-based relay control setup.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the [product_name] to work and be configurable regardless of the SIM PIN's status, as the documentation suggests. They also look for clear feedback on errors and accessible guidance for controlling relay outputs via SMS.
